The [Profit Margin Calculator](/profit-margin-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Gross margin, markup and profit from cost and price. Enter your cost and selling price and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Profit margin is the share of the selling price you keep as profit. Markup is profit as a share of cost. Mixing the two up is one of the most common pricing mistakes. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the Profit Margin Calculator

Start by entering your cost, then entering your selling price. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your cost.
2. Enter your selling price.
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Margin = (Price − Cost) ÷ Price × 100. Markup = (Price − Cost) ÷ Cost × 100.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Profit Margin Calculator](/profit-margin-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. An item costing 40 sold for 65 earns 25 profit: a 38.46% margin and a 62.5% markup. Try the same figures in the [Profit Margin Calculator](/profit-margin-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Cost: 40, Selling price: 65), the [Profit Margin Calculator](/profit-margin-calculator) returns Profit margin: 38.46%, Profit: 25, Markup: 62.5%. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- A 50% markup is only a 33% margin.
- Include shipping, fees and returns in cost.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What's the difference between margin and markup?

Margin divides profit by price; markup divides profit by cost. Markup is always the larger number. Try it with your own numbers in the [Profit Margin Calculator](/profit-margin-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is a good profit margin?

It varies widely by industry — retail is often 2–10% net, software can exceed 20%. Try it with your own numbers in the [Profit Margin Calculator](/profit-margin-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Profit Margin Calculator use?

Margin = (Price − Cost) ÷ Price × 100. Markup = (Price − Cost) ÷ Cost × 100. You can see it in action in the [Profit Margin Calculator](/profit-margin-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

Just Cost and Selling price. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
